calendarNotes: Collier County Public Schools starts the 2026-2027 school year for students on Tuesday, August 11, 2026 and ends the student year on Thursday, May 27, 2027 with early dismissal and the end of Quarter 4. Teachers start August 4 and the last teacher day is May 28. Fall Break runs November 23-27, Winter Break runs December 21-January 4 with students returning January 5, and Spring Break runs March 22-29 with classes resuming March 30. The official calendar totals 180 student days and 196 teacher days, and the district also publishes Spanish and Creole calendar PDFs.

calendarFaqs.q: When does Collier County school start in 2026?
calendarFaqs.a: The first student day for Collier County Public Schools is Tuesday, August 11, 2026.

calendarFaqs.q: When is the last day of school for Collier County in 2027?
calendarFaqs.a: The last student day is Thursday, May 27, 2027. It is also listed as an early dismissal day and the end of Quarter 4.

calendarFaqs.q: When is Collier County Spring Break in 2027?
calendarFaqs.a: Spring Break runs March 22-29, 2027, with classes resuming Tuesday, March 30.

calendarFaqs.q: When is Winter Break for Collier County schools in 2026-2027?
calendarFaqs.a: Winter Break runs Monday, December 21, 2026 through Monday, January 4, 2027. Students return Tuesday, January 5, 2027.

calendarFaqs.q: When is Collier County Fall Break in 2026?
calendarFaqs.a: Fall Break runs Monday, November 23 through Friday, November 27, 2026.

calendarFaqs.q: Does Collier County have early dismissal days in 2026-2027?
calendarFaqs.a: Yes. The official 2026-2027 Collier academic calendar lists early dismissal and professional learning dates, including August 26, October 29, February 2, April 21, May 21, and the final student day on May 27.

calendarFaqs.q: Does Collier publish Spanish and Creole calendars for 2026-2027?
calendarFaqs.a: Yes. Collier County Public Schools publishes Spanish and Creole versions of the 2026-2027 academic calendar, linked as alternate official calendars on this page.

calendarFaqs.q: How many student and teacher days are in the Collier 2026-2027 calendar?
calendarFaqs.a: The official calendar totals 180 student days and 196 teacher days.

customSections.label: Collier Calendar Decision Guide: How Families Can Plan Around School Dates
customSections.content: The CCPS calendar is most useful when families treat it as a decision guide, not just a holiday list. The largest scheduling windows for Collier families are the August start period, Fall Break, Winter Break, Spring Break, and late-May early dismissal and graduation-week dates.

groups.label: Before school starts
items: Use the August start window to confirm registration, transportation, supplies, and first-week routines.
Check whether your household needs the English, Spanish, or Creole official calendar PDF.
Review early dismissal and teacher planning dates before setting childcare routines for the first quarter.

groups.label: During major breaks
items: Fall Break overlaps Thanksgiving travel and can require early childcare planning.
Winter Break is the longest family scheduling window during Collier's busy winter season.
Spring Break affects travel, childcare, camps, and seasonal work schedules across Naples, Marco Island, Immokalee, and inland communities.

groups.label: End-of-year planning
items: Late May includes early dismissal and graduation-week signals before the final student day.
Families should verify school-specific graduation, testing, and campus event calendars before making summer travel plans.

customSections.label: Collier Calendar Track Information
customSections.content: This page summarizes the Collier County Public Schools 2026-2027 traditional academic calendar. Individual schools, athletics, testing, graduation week details, activity schedules, and hurricane-related changes may be published separately, so families should verify campus-specific dates with CCPS.

customSections.label: Important Collier Academic Planning Dates
customSections.content: Several CCPS dates matter even when they are not labeled as major holidays. These academic planning signals help families understand when schedules may change, when students may not attend, and when school-specific follow-up is needed.

groups.label: Dates beyond holidays
items: Quarter ending dates appear October 9, December 18, March 18, and May 27.
Teacher plan or professional development days include September 21, October 12, January 4, March 19, and May 28.
Early dismissal and professional learning dates include August 26, October 29, February 2, April 21, May 21, and May 27.
FTE periods begin October 5 and February 8, which can matter for district reporting and attendance awareness.
Graduation week appears near the May 21 early dismissal date; final graduation details should be verified with individual schools.

customSections.label: Understanding the CCPS Calendar
customSections.content: The official CCPS calendar includes planning terms that matter even when they are not major breaks. Understanding those terms helps families read the calendar correctly and avoid confusing student attendance days with staff workdays, reporting periods, or school-level events.

groups.label: Calendar terms families should know
items: Teacher Planning Days: students may not attend while teachers complete scheduled planning work.
Professional Development Days: staff training or professional learning may change student schedules.
Early Dismissal Days: pickup, childcare, bus timing, and after-school routines may need adjustment.
Quarter Ending Dates: grading periods, report card timing, and academic checkpoints follow these milestones.
Interim Dates: progress updates or academic checkpoints may be published during the school year.
Report Card Dates: these are academic milestones when families review student progress after a grading period.
FTE Periods: these dates appear for district reporting and attendance awareness, not as major holiday breaks.

customSections.label: Collier School Calendar FAQ by Community
customSections.content: Families often search for school calendars by city or community name. CCPS publishes the main academic calendar districtwide, but school-level events, testing, athletics, graduation, and specialized programs may have separate details.

columns: How to use the CCPS calendar
rows: Use the CCPS district calendar for holidays, breaks, and student days; pay extra attention to Winter Break, Spring Break, graduation-week schedules, and school-specific campus events.
Use the districtwide CCPS academic calendar and confirm travel-sensitive events, travel timing, and campus activities with the assigned school.
Use the CCPS calendar for districtwide dates and check school-specific transportation, program, and event updates, especially when early dismissal or teacher planning days affect longer commutes.
Use the CCPS calendar for districtwide no-school days and account for longer commute or bus timing on early dismissal, professional learning, and major break transition days.
Use the district calendar as the school-year baseline and verify school-level events before making travel, childcare, or end-of-year plans.
